notes:
Need to search first.I wasn't able to research this chapter, so I have no notes to give you on Esther 4.

My first try to open the commentary pages (Enduring Word, BibleHub, Precept Austin and StudyLight) didn't work. The tool will only open a page after a search has returned its link, and I tried to open the links directly. When I then ran the searches, I had used up my tool calls for this turn, so nothing came back.

Your rules say to report only what the pages I actually read say, and I haven't read any. Notes written from memory would break that rule, so I've left them out rather than invent content or URLs.

If you send the request again, I'll start with searches and then read the pages they find. The plan:

- **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word on Esther 4, the BibleHub verse pages (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit, Matthew Henry, Benson), StudyLight, and Precept Austin's Esther 4 page.
- **Where Protestant traditions differ:** Reformed writers (Ligonier, The Gospel Coalition) on God working out of sight in v. 14, and Baptist writers (Desiring God, Spurgeon) on v. 14 and v. 16. For Methodists, Wesley's notes at wesley.nnu.edu. For Pentecostals, Enduring Word or ag.org on the fast in v. 16. For Lutherans, lcms.org and 1517.org, including Luther's views on the book of Esther.
- **Other views:** NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey for modern scholarship. New Advent and catholic.com on the Greek additions to Esther, which add prayers by Mordecai and Esther around this chapter. GotQuestions on how "for such a time as this" (v. 14) is used, and sometimes misused, in popular teaching.
